maria: Quick sync — FlashFusion (v2/v3 mix) rollout readiness. Found two perf regressions when switching kernel for short sequences (seq<=64). Need to settle on kernel-selection heuristics, batching defaults, and KV eviction policy. Can we triage today? /cc @devon @sasha

devon: I ran a tight profiler yesterday. Key points:
- seq=32: v2 (current) = 1.20k tok/s, v3 = 1.10k tok/s (v3 wins only after seq>=96)
- seq=128: v2 = 950 tok/s, v3 = 1.14k tok/s (~1.2x)
- Observed extra cudaMemcpy in v3 path on short seqs -> kernel chooser currently prefers v3 incorrectly

Profiler snippet:
```
Model: gpt-medium | batch=8 | seq=32
v2: throughput=1200 tok/s | kernel_time=18ms | memcpy=1ms
v3: throughput=1100 tok/s | kernel_time=12ms | memcpy=9ms <-- memcpy penalty
```

sasha: Agree we need flags separated. Proposal:
- feature.flashfusion.enabled (master toggle)
- feature.flashfusion.kernel_chooser=v2|v3|auto
- feature.flashfusion.paged_attention=on|off
- feature.flashfusion.fused_kernels=on|off
Would keep auto as default until we have safe heuristics. Thoughts? :eyes:

aj: Rollout suggestion:
1) Canary in us-west: 1% traffic (24h) -> watch p50/p95 latency, error rate
2) Gradual to 10% (48h) with auto-fallback to v2 on latency regression
3) Region expansion w/ 1% in eu-west then 10%
4) If KV evictions spike, pause and rollback
I'll own the rollout doc + monitoring playbook. :+1:

leo: KV cache note: under high concurrency the paged-KV eviction loop is thrashing; we see 20-30ms spikes when the eviction runs during generation. Two quick mitigations:
- increase soft_limit from 70% -> 85% of cache memory
- stagger eviction sweeps with randomized jitter
Command to repro and trace:
```
./tools/run_kv_profiler --clients 200 --seq 256 --warmup 30s --log kv_trace.json
```
I can try soft_limit bump in staging and rebench.
